newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: OPINION-Czech president changes style, By Jiri Peh.
newsitem.headline: OPINION-Czech president changes style, By Jiri Peh.

text.p: PRAGUE, April 10 - President Vaclav Havel has, since undergoing cancer surgery last December, become more vociferous in expressing his misgivings about various Czech political and social ills.
Havel as a politician who is perceived as more "human" is also likely to be more listened to. His new style, which some commentators see as a weakness, thus may be his strength.
The change in style coincides with his recovery from critical cancer surgery in December.

Although Havel said after the surgery that, in facing death, he had reordered his life priorities, it seems his changing political behavior is also connected to the worsening political climate in the country.
In recent weeks, Havel has harshly criticized politicians, including parliamentary chairman Milos Zeman, for what he saw as irresponsible acts.
He has spoken about "the suffocating atmosphere" in society, putting much of the blame on a bad political culture among both opposition and coalition politicians.

After his return from vacation in Belgium in February, Havel told Czechs they tend to have inflated opinions of themselves. Abroad, he argued, the country is often perceived as a place where you can get easily robbed or pickpocketted.

Havel's recent statement to the French daily Le Figaro describing Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar as "paranoid" is something that would have been difficult to hear from the cautious president only six months ago. His statement has further strained already cold Czech-Slovak relations.
